title: How the web works
subtitle: Type a URL, press Enter — and a dozen systems cooperate in under a second. Follow one request all the way.

url.title: URLs and clients/servers
url.body: The web is a client–server system: a browser (client) requests resources from a web server. A URL such as https://example.com:443/docs?page=2#top has scheme (protocol), host, port, path, query string and fragment. The fragment never leaves the browser.

dns.title: DNS: names to addresses
dns.body: Computers route by IP address, so the browser first asks DNS to resolve the host name. The answer is cached at several levels (browser, OS, resolver) for its TTL, so repeat visits skip the lookup.

http.title: HTTP request and response
http.body: HTTP is a text protocol: the client sends a request (method, path, headers, optional body); the server answers with a response (status code, headers, body). Methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE. Status families: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error. HTTP is stateless: each request stands alone; cookies and tokens carry identity.

latency.title: Why latency matters
latency.body: Each round trip costs the network RTT. A page needing DNS (1 RTT), TCP (1), TLS (1–2), then the request (1) needs about 4–5 RTTs before the first byte. HTTP/2 multiplexes requests on one connection; HTTP/3 uses QUIC to cut handshakes.
latency.steps: RTT = 50 ms. Steps: DNS, TCP, TLS, request = 4 round trips. Time to first byte ≥ 4 × 50 ms.

html.title: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
html.body: HTML is structure (headings, links, forms); CSS is presentation (layout, colour); JavaScript is behaviour. The browser parses HTML into the DOM tree, CSS into a style tree, combines them to lay out and paint. Keep the three separate so each can change alone.

static.title: Static, dynamic and SPA
static.body: Static sites serve the same files to all; dynamic sites build pages per request on the server; single-page apps (SPAs) load one page and update it with JavaScript, fetching JSON. SPAs feel fast after first load but cost a heavy first load and need care for SEO.
